words.gram: m. nom. pl. pres. part. mid. adhi-√i

hindi: और जो भी हमसे सम्बद्ध, अवश्य भरण-पोषण करने योग्य, वे लक्षण, अंगविद्या, जम्भकविद्या, माया-गत, आश्रम-धर्म, निमित्त, अन्तर-चक्र का अध्ययन करने वाले गुप्तचर, और संसर्गविद्या को
english: And also those who are connected with us and are to be maintained without fail — they, studying lakṣaṇa (marks), the science of limbs, the jambhaka science, māyā-gata, the dharma of the āśramas, omens and the antara-cakra, [are] secret agents; and the science of association.
notes: 'asmabandhinaḥ' is read asma- (the compound form of asmad, 'we, our') + bandhin, 'connected with us'; sense doubtful (the printed asma- is unusual; no change made). The list lakṣaṇa ... antara-cakra is closed by iti (not rendered, a list closer, not a quotation); lakṣaṇa, māyā-gata and antara-cakra are kept as technical terms, no sense imported. jambhaka-vidyā as in the glossary (13.2). 'saṃsarga-vidyāṃ ca' is an accusative left hanging after the comma: it appears to continue the list governed by adhīyānāḥ ('and [studying] the science of association'), but it is translated literally without supplying a verb. The sentence is verbless in te ... sattriṇaḥ (copula supplied in brackets in English only). Unit 1 of the chapter continues in the same style as unit 2 (te tīkṣṇāḥ).

words.gram: tat-puruṣa, m. abl./gen. sg. as ind.

hindi: जो जनपद में शूर, अपने को त्याग देने वाले, धन के हेतु हाथी या हिंस्र पशु से लड़ें, वे तीक्ष्ण
english: Those who in the country are brave, who have abandoned themselves, and would fight against an elephant or a beast of prey for the sake of property — they [are] assassins (tīkṣṇa).
notes: pratiyodhayeyuḥ is formally a causative (literally 'would cause to fight against'); rendered 'fight against' as is usual for this verb. dravya = property/valuables, so the compound could also be 'for the sake of wealth'. tyakta-ātman 'one who has abandoned himself' (regardless of life), kept literal. jana-pada here 'in the country' (the territory).

hindi: जो बन्धुओं में स्नेह से रहित, क्रूर और आलसी, वे विष देने वाले
english: Those who among relatives are without affection, cruel and lazy — they [are] poisoners (rasada).
notes: 'nihsnehāḥ' shows the e-text's h for visarga before a sibilant (habit, no flag). rasada = poisoner (rasa = poison in this sense).

hindi: परिव्राजिका, जीविका चाहने वाली, दरिद्र, विधवा, प्रगल्भ, ब्राह्मणी, अन्तःपुर में सत्कार पाई हुई, महामात्रों के कुलों के पास जाए
english: A parivrājikā, desiring livelihood, poor, a widow, bold, a Brahmin woman, honoured in the inner apartments, should approach the families of high officials.
notes: The adjectives (vṛtti-kāmā ... kṛta-satkārā) are read as describing the parivrājikā, with no ca; they could also be separate kinds of women, but the singular verb favours one person. vṛtti = livelihood (not 'maintenance'). kṛta-satkārā literally 'by whom honour has been made'.

hindi: इससे मुण्डाओं, वृषलियों की व्याख्या की गई। ये सञ्चार हैं।
english: By this the shaven-headed [women], the vṛṣalīs, are explained. Such are the sañcāras (literally 'goings-about').

text_flags.suggest: | 5 | (end of sentence 5; 'iti sañcārāḥ' may head the next unit)
text_flags.why: embedded verse-number marker inside a unit; grouping to be checked against the edition

notes: GROUPING: the embedded '| 5 |' marks the end of edition sentence 5; 'iti sañcārāḥ' is a closing label that sums up the preceding sentences (the movers described so far) and is kept with this unit. The verse number is not rendered. muṇḍā vṛṣalyaḥ have no ca: read as two items; the alternative is 'shaven-headed vṛṣalīs' (muṇḍā as an adjective). vṛṣalī is kept as a term (a śūdra woman in the usual sense). iti is glossed 'closing particle'.

words.gloss: assembly of counsellors, superintendent, army, fort, frontier officer, forest chief (end of the long compound)
having credible place, dress, skill, language and high birth as pretexts

hindi: राजा उन विश्वसनीय स्थान, वेश, शिल्प, भाषा, कुल के बहाने वालों को अपने देश में मन्त्री, पुरोहित, सेनापति, युवराज, दौवारिक, अन्तर्वंशिक, प्रशास्ता, समाहर्ता, सन्निधाता, प्रदेष्टा, नायक, नगरवासी, व्यावहारिक, कार्मान्तिक, मन्त्रि-परिषद्, अध्यक्ष, सेना, दुर्ग, अन्तपाल, आटविकों में भक्ति से और सामर्थ्य के योग से अपसर्पण कराए।
english: The king should cause them — those whose pretexts are credible place, dress, skill, language and high birth — to go away in his own territory among the counsellors, the chaplain, the commander of the army, the heir-apparent, the dauvārika, the antarvaṃśika, the praśāstṛ, the Collector, the Treasurer, the pradeṣṭṛs, the leaders, the townsmen, the vyāvahārikas, the kārmāntikas, the assembly of counsellors, the superintendents, the army, the fort, the frontier officers and the forest chiefs, out of devotion and by connection with capacity.
notes: The long locative dvandva is split across three tokens by the e-text's line-end continuation marks ('.-'): each token carries its members, the case ending is on the last token. daṇḍa and durga are taken literally (army, fort); an elided -pāla ('commander of the army, fort-guardian') is possible. dauvārika (literally 'of the door') and antarvaṃśika are kept as titles/terms; pradeṣṭṛ, vyāvahārika, kārmāntika kept as in the glossary. The pretext compound (śraddheya ... apadeśa) is read as a bahuvrīhi qualifying tān, 'whose pretexts are credible place, dress, ...'; it could also be read as 'with pretexts of place, dress ... which are credible'. apasarpayet is the causative of apa-√sṛp, rendered literally 'cause to go away' (the sense 'send out as spies' being implied by apasarpa = spy). bhaktitaḥ 'out of devotion' (alternative: according to devotion). yoga here 'connection'.

words.gloss: takers-up of parasol, bhṛṅgāra, fan, sandals, seat, vehicle and conveyance

hindi: छत्र, भृङ्गार, पंखा, पादुका, आसन, यान, वाहन को ग्रहण करने वाले तीक्ष्ण उनके बाहरी चर को जानें।
english: The assassins who take up the parasol, the bhṛṅgāra, the fan, the sandals, the seat, the vehicle and the conveyance should know their external spy.
notes: cāra = spy (glossary 9.5), here a collective singular ('spying'); 'external' because the next unit gives the internal one. bhṛṅgāra is kept as a term (a vessel). upagrāhin 'one who takes up/holds' kept literal; whether it means carrying the objects for the officers is not stated.

hindi: गुप्तचर उसे संस्थाओं में सौंपें।
english: The secret agents should hand him over to the saṃsthās.
notes: saṃsthā is kept untranslated (the organized establishment of spies, as the later units show); 'him' is the person whose external spy has been learned in the previous unit.

words.gloss: cook, ārālika, bath-attendant, rubber, bed-spreader, kalpaka, prasādhaka, water

words.gloss: having the disguise of hunchback, dwarf, Kirāta, dumb, deaf, dull and blind
actor, dancer, singer, instrumentalist, those living by speech, kuśīlavas

hindi: रसोइया, आरालिक, स्नान कराने वाले, रगड़ने वाले, बिछौना बिछाने वाले, कल्पक, प्रसाधक, जल के परिचारक, विष देने वाले, कुबड़े, बौने, किरात, गूँगे, बहरे, जड़, अन्धे के छद्म वाले, नट, नर्तक, गायक, वादक, वाणी से जीविका चलाने वाले, कुशीलव, स्त्रियाँ भीतरी चर को जानें।
english: The cooks, ārālikas, bath-attendants, rubbers, bed-spreaders, kalpakas, prasādhakas, water-attendants, poisoners, those in the disguise of hunchbacks, dwarfs, Kirātas, the dumb, the deaf, the dull and the blind, actors, dancers, singers, instrumentalists, those who live by speech, kuśīlavas and women should know the internal spy.
notes: The first compound is split across two tokens by the e-text's line-end '.-': members in token 1, the final member paricāraka ('udaka-paricārakāḥ', water-attendants) in token 2. ārālika, kalpaka, prasādhaka, kuśīlava kept untranslated (glossary); snāpaka bath-attendant, saṃvāhaka rubber, āstaraka bed-spreader as in 7.17. The list has no ca until the last ('striyaḥ ca'); in Hindi it takes commas only. chadman is read as the last member of a bahuvrīhi, 'having the guise of hunchbacks ... the blind'; the e-text 'andhac.chadmāno' has the doubled c as written. kirāta is a tribe name, kept. jaḍa literally 'dull'. rasada = poisoner.

hindi: भिक्षुकियाँ उसे संस्थाओं में सौंपें।
english: The female mendicants should hand him over to the saṃsthās.

text_flags.why: missing u; bhikṣukī (f.), nom. pl. bhikṣukyaḥ, as in unit 13 bhikṣukī-pratiṣedhe
likely typo (p/r transposed); unit 8 has arpayeyuḥ in the parallel sentence

notes: Parallel to unit 8 with the hand-over done by female mendicants. Both typos are kept in src and corrected in words.

hindi: संस्थाओं के शिष्य संज्ञाओं और लिपियों से चर का संचार करें।
english: The pupils of the saṃsthās should effect the circulation of the spy by signs and writings.
notes: cāra-sañcāra literally 'the going-about of the spy' (the passing of spy business); the sense of communication is not stated. antevāsin = pupil (literally 'dweller near').

hindi: और संस्थाएँ अथवा वे एक-दूसरे को न जानें।
english: And the saṃsthās or they should not know one another.
notes: te ('they') is probably the pupils of the previous unit; vā is rendered 'or' (the sense 'neither ... nor' is a possible reading). Scope of na: negates vidyuḥ.

words.gloss: in the guise of mother and father
by song, recitation, instrumental music, wares, secret writing and signs

hindi: भिक्षुकियों का निषेध होने पर द्वारपालों की परम्परा, माता-पिता के वेश वाले, शिल्प करने वाली, कुशीलव अथवा दासियाँ, अथवा गीत, पाठ, वाद्य, माल, गूढ़ लेख, संकेतों से चर को बाहर ले जाएँ।
english: When female mendicants are prohibited, a succession of doorkeepers, those in the guise of mother and father, female practitioners of skill, kuśīlavas or female slaves, or by song, recitation, instrumental music, wares, secret writing and signs, should carry out the spy.

text_flags.why: possible: a nominative singular does not agree with the plural verb nirhareyuḥ; the instrumental paramparayā ('through a succession of doorkeepers') or plural paramparāḥ would be expected. Doubtful.

notes: dvāhstha = dvāḥstha (e-text h for visarga before a sibilant, habit). The final '.' of the token is the e-text's full stop. The syntax is loose: the nominatives (doorkeeper succession, those in the guise of parents, skilled women, kuśīlavas, female slaves) are the persons who carry out the spy; the instrumentals are the means; the sense 'by means of a succession of doorkeepers' is possible. gīta-pāṭhya-vādya-bhāṇḍa-gūḍha-lekhya-sañjñā is read as a dvandva of six; bhāṇḍa 'wares' may go with gūḍha-lekhya ('secret writing in wares'): doubtful. nir-√hṛ 'carry out' as in the glossary (7.17). mātā-pitṛ-vyañjanāḥ: bahuvrīhi 'in the guise of mother and father', no 'agents' added.

words.gloss: by the release of long illness, madness, fire and poison

hindi: दीर्घ रोग, उन्माद, अग्नि, विष के विसर्ग से अथवा गूढ़ निर्गमन।
english: Or by the release of long illness, madness, fire and poison, [there is] a secret going out.
notes: visarga (here 'letting go/release') is kept literal; it may mean sending forth or pretending, and applies to all four items or perhaps only the last (alternatives). rasa = poison. The clause is verbless (copula bracketed in English only).

hindi: तीन के एक वाक्य में विश्वास।
english: Of three, in one statement, [is] confidence.
notes: Verbless; 'of three' has no noun (three reports/agents are implied); eka-vākya literally 'one statement' (agreement). sampratyaya 'confidence/assurance' (alternative: conviction).

hindi: उनके बार-बार पतन होने पर मौन दण्ड निषेध।
english: Of them, in frequent fall, silent punishment [is] prohibition.
notes: vinipāta 'falling, ruin' (failure) kept literal; daṇḍa = punishment. The clause is verbless; pratiṣedha 'prohibition' (alternative: restraint, prevention).

words.gloss: spoken of in the cleansing of thorns
for the purpose of the spy

hindi: और कण्टकशोधन में कहे गए गुप्तचर दूसरों में वेतन निर्धारित किए हुए, न मिलने वाले, चर के प्रयोजन से रहें।
english: And the secret agents spoken of in the cleansing of thorns, with pay made, should dwell among the others, not coming together, for the purpose of the spy.
notes: kaṇṭaka-śodhana = cleansing of thorns (literal; the reference is to the treatise section so named). apasarpa = spy/secret agent. kṛta-vetana literally 'with pay made'. asampātin: obscure, literal 'not falling/coming together' (alternatives: not moving about, not visiting); low confidence. pareṣu 'among the others'. cāra-artham 'for the sake of the spy'.

hindi: वे दोनों से वेतन पाने वाले।
english: They [are] those paid by both.
notes: ta = te by sandhi before a vowel. ubhaya-vetana = one paid by both (glossary 9.6); 'both' is not specified (the two kings).

hindi: और दोनों से वेतन पाने वालों को ग्रहीत पुत्रों और पत्नियों वाला करे। और उन्हें शत्रु द्वारा भेजे हुए जाने, और उनकी शुचिता तद्विधों से।
english: And [one] should make those paid by both into [men] whose sons and wives are taken. And he should know them [as] sent by the enemy, and their purity [he should know] by those of that kind.
notes: Two-line verse. 'Taken' (gṛhīta) is kept literal (held; the sense of keeping sons and wives as pledge is not stated). The last clause 'teṣāṃ śaucaṃ ca tadvidhaiḥ' has no verb: vidyāt is understood (bracketed in English, left verbless in Hindi). tad-vidha 'of that kind' (probably other agents of the same sort). ari = enemy. The first ca of line b joins the clauses; the second joins 'their purity'.

hindi: इस प्रकार शत्रु में, मित्र में, मध्यम में, उदासीन में, उनके अठारह तीर्थों में भी चरों को डाले।
english: In this way [one] should sow spies in the enemy, in the ally, in the middle, in the neutral and in their eighteen tīrthas also.
notes: madhyama and udāsīna are the middle and the neutral king (glossary 6.2/7.2). āvapet (ā-√vap) literally 'sow, scatter' (usually 'plant'). cara = spy (agent). tīrtha kept (the eighteen offices of the state; sense in notes only). The five ca's join the members of one list; Hindi uses commas only.

hindi: उनके भीतरी घर में विचरने वाले कुबड़े, बौने, नपुंसक, शिल्पवती स्त्रियाँ, गूँगे और विविध म्लेच्छ जातियाँ।
english: Their goers in the inner house [are] hunchbacks, dwarfs and eunuchs, skilled women, the dumb and various mleccha kinds.
notes: antar-gṛha-cara 'one who goes about in the inner house' (spy of the inner house). paṇḍaka = eunuch (usual sense). citrāḥ 'various' agrees with mleccha-jātayaḥ; mūkāḥ is masculine plural and stands as a separate item; the grouping of the list (ca only before the last item) is read as one list. jāti = kind/birth. mleccha kept as a name in the compound.

words.gloss: at the end of the fort
at the end of the country

hindi: दुर्गों में वणिक् संस्थाएँ, दुर्ग के अन्त में सिद्ध और तापस, किसान और उदास्थित राष्ट्र में, राष्ट्र के अन्त में व्रज में रहने वाले।
english: In the forts, merchants [are] the saṃsthās; at the end of the fort, holy men and ascetics; farmers and udāsthitas in the country; at the end of the country, dwellers in cattle-stations.
notes: saṃsthā is saṃsthāḥ by regular sandhi (āḥ before a voiced consonant). The sentence is elliptical: the saṃsthās are merchants in forts, and so on; the verbless parts are supplied only by a bracketed copula in English. siddha = holy man, tāpasa = ascetic; udāsthita is kept as a term (not explained); vraja = cattle-station.

words.gloss: śramaṇas, forest chiefs and the like
having the knowledge of the other's activity as purpose

hindi: वन में वनचर करने योग्य, श्रमण, आटविक आदि। दूसरे की प्रवृत्ति को जानने के प्रयोजन वाली शीघ्र चर-परम्पराएँ।
english: In the forest forest-goers are to be made — śramaṇas, forest chiefs and the like; for knowing the other's activity, swift successions of spies [are to be made].

text_flags.why: stray dot (compound dot) in place of a space after śīghrāś, which is a separate word (śīghrāḥ ca-)

notes: The second line has no verb: kāryāḥ is carried over (bracketed in English only). The token is flagged: śīghrāḥ is a separate adjective, not part of the compound. para = 'the other' (not rendered 'enemy'). śramaṇa kept as a term; ādi 'and the like'.

words.gloss: by those of such a kind

hindi: और दूसरे के ये तादृश लोगों से ही जानने योग्य, तादृश। चर का संचार करने वाले, संस्थाएँ, गूढ़, अगूढ़ नाम वाले।
english: And these of the other are to be known only by those of such a kind — [they being] of such a kind. [They are] circulators of the spy, saṃsthās, secret ones, and those named not secret.
notes: Very terse and doubtful: 'tādṛśaiḥ eva tādṛśāḥ' read as 'those of such a kind [are to be known] only by those of such a kind'; line b lists four kinds (cāra-sañcārin, saṃsthā, gūḍha, agūḍha-sañjñita), the ca joining the last two. saṃsthā = saṃsthāḥ by sandhi. agūḍha-sañjñita literally 'named/called not-secret'. cāra-sañcārin literally 'one who circulates the spy / moves about with the spy'. The Hindi list takes commas only (no final और).

words.gloss: by those of the party of the seducible
for the purpose of knowing the other's spies

hindi: अकृत्य, कृत्यपक्ष वालों द्वारा कार्य के कारणों से दिखाए गए मुखियों को दूसरे के गुप्तचरों को जानने के प्रयोजन से अन्तों में बसाए।
english: [One] should lodge at the frontiers, for the purpose of knowing the other's spies, the chiefs — unseducible, shown by those of the party of the seducible through reasons of business.
notes: akṛtya = unseducible (opposite of kṛtya-pakṣa, glossary 12.3/9.3). darśita 'shown' (represented/pointed out) kept literal; kārya-hetu 'reason of business' is obscure (pretexts of the task). anta literally 'end' (frontier, as in anta-pāla). Subject of vāsayet is unstated.
